answer: A voyage-based reputation bond can resist sybils: before an agent may trade, it must stake a refundable deposit that vests only after a sustained history of honest transactions, like a slow voyage rather than a single trip. Each identity's stake sits on a ledge — one proven fraud tips it off and the deposit is slashed. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital per identity, while a zephyr of cheap, disposable accounts blows away because none can afford the bond or survive long enough to earn it back.
